games.title: Artist's Tool Box
games.skillName: Naming art tools and what they do
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to use drawing, painting and sculpture to develop and share their ideas, experiences and imagination
games.instruction: Read the question, then tap the best answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what each tool is used for.

questions.ask: What do you dip in paint to make a painting?
What do you use to draw thin grey lines?
What do you use to rub out a pencil mistake?
Which soft material can you squeeze and shape into a model?
Where do artists mix their paints?
What stands up to hold a painting while the artist works?
What is a 3D artwork you can walk all round called?
Which is best for drawing on the playground outside?

games.title: Shape Spotter
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to develop a wide range of art and design techniques in using colour, pattern, texture, line, shape, form and space
games.instruction: Read the clues, then tap who or what it is.
games.hint: Not quite. Count the sides and corners in the clues.

questions.ask: I have 3 straight sides and 3 corners. What am I?
I am perfectly round and have no corners. What am I?
I have 4 equal sides and 4 corners. What am I?
I have 4 sides: 2 long sides and 2 short sides. What am I?
I have 5 points and twinkle in the night sky in pictures. What am I?
I am like a stretched circle, the shape of an egg. What am I?
I have 6 sides, like a cell in a honeycomb. What am I?
I am drawn on cards to show love. What am I?

games.title: Collage Creator
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to use a range of materials creatively to design and make products
games.instruction: Read the sentence, then tap True or False.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what you do when you make a collage.

questions.ask: A collage is a picture made by sticking things down.
You can use torn paper in a collage.
A collage can only be made with paint.
Leaves and scraps of fabric can go in a collage.
Clay goes hard when it dries out.
Thin paper is stronger than thick card.
You should wash your brush before using a new colour.
Wool and buttons can never be used in art.

games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to use drawing, painting and sculpture to develop and share their ideas, experiences and imagination

questions.ask: Which colours could show a happy, sunny day?

games.hint: Not quite. Think about what each maker works with.

questions.ask: Who makes pots and bowls from clay?
Who designs buildings?
Who makes cloth by weaving threads?

Who paints pictures on paper or canvas?
Who makes pictures with a camera?
Who designs new clothes?

games.title: Meet the Artists
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught about the work of a range of artists, craft makers and designers, describing the differences and similarities between different practices and disciplines, and making links to their own work
games.instruction: Read the clues, then tap who or what it is.
games.hint: Not quite. Read the clue again and think about the famous picture.

questions.ask: I painted 'Sunflowers' and 'The Starry Night'. Who am I?
I painted the water lilies in my garden pond in France. Who am I?
When I was old, I cut out bright paper shapes to make pictures. Who am I?
I am a Mexican artist famous for self-portraits with flowers. Who am I?
I make art outdoors from leaves, sticks and stones. Who am I?
I love polka dots and cover whole rooms in them. Who am I?
I painted busy northern towns full of 'matchstick' people. Who am I?
I made 'The Great Wave', a famous Japanese print. Who am I?
